_description:
# compact: keep what you need to go on after agent-fsm history is folded

This is for an agent-fsm body. When you see a user message starting with `[aos] compact:` asking for a summary, answer with that summary and nothing else. You have no tools for that one answer. Do not finish or abandon the work just because a summary was requested.

Right before that request, the body clears old tool outputs to make the request smaller: their content becomes one line, `[aos] tool output cleared (N chars from TOOL); the original is in history_removed.jsonl`, and the request says how many were cleared. Your own messages, your tool calls with their arguments, the last three tool outputs, the results of your last group of tool calls, and outputs shorter than 300 characters stay as they are. Write the summary from what you said and did about each output; if an exact value from a cleared output matters, say where it came from (file, path, tool) so you can look it up again.

Write everything you will need to continue: who asked for what, letter names and where to reply, what is done, what you are in the middle of, the next step, everything still open, important files and paths, the rules and decisions you must keep following, and your todo and goal. Keep exact identifiers and paths. Letters you have not answered yet will stay unchanged, but the rest of your working context depends on your summary.

After that answer, the body replaces the earlier conversation with one user message starting `[aos] summary:`, then an assistant `compact done: ...` answering only the /compact letters, then the user messages it kept, including unanswered letters in their original form. If compaction interrupted work in progress, the body also appends a user message `[aos] compact: done. Go on with the work in progress described in the summary above; letters you have not answered yet are above.` This is a continuation instruction: resume the work, not another request to summarize.

The originals are in `<stack>/history_removed.jsonl`. Your summary is also appended to `<stack>/handoff.md`, one section per compaction. Your todo and goal are not changed. Rules and controls: `aos/me/compact.json#/rules`.
rules:
# compact: rules and controls

- `/compact` is a body command sent to your own `<stack>/queue`, not your mailbox. A human or a hook can send it. If you have the optional events pack, you can request it with `clock_register` `{"op":"add","name":"compact_once","after":1,"text":"/compact"}` (no box means your own queue). The stock agent-fsm tools do not include events. Do not pretend you can send it when you have no such tool. Extra instructions may follow `/compact` after whitespace.
- The body can accept /compact during a turn once all tool results have arrived. It does not deliver ordinary new letters to you mid-turn. While a summary is being requested, idle takes no new letters. /compact bypasses before_queue and after_queue hooks.
- Fewer than four foldable messages (not counting user messages that must stay) means no brain call and nothing folded: the body answers the /compact letters with one assistant message `compact not needed: only N messages to fold (it takes at least 4); nothing was folded` (aos.compact and aos.skipped are true), and ask/listen get that answer. Such answers do not count as foldable, so sending /compact again right after a compact gets the same answer. For /compact, a dropped `failed` letter now means a failed summary only; ask/listen sees LetterDropped.
- Clearing old tool outputs happens on every /compact that asks for a summary, before the request is added; a /compact answered `compact not needed` clears nothing. Each cleared original goes to history_removed.jsonl as `{removed_at, op: "clear_tools", line, message}`, and compact.json records `cleared` and `cleared_chars`. Outputs already cleared are not cleared again. If history keeps changing or cannot be read, the body skips clearing with one warning and asks for the summary as before.
- Hooks before_compact and after_compact (your stock definition hooks nothing on them; a program hooked there can change how you are compacted). before_compact runs when a /compact has enough to fold, before old tool outputs are cleared: it can block it (the /compact letters get one answer `compact blocked by hook H: ...; nothing was folded`, with aos.skipped and aos.blocked; in the middle of a turn the letters wait until the turn ends and it runs again), change the extra instructions you get, keep old tool outputs, or give a summary itself (then you are not asked and the next thing you see is the folded history). after_compact runs when the summary is ready, before history is rewritten: it can change the summary or give text to add back, which you see as one user message `[aos] restored after compact: ...` right after the summary; it is not a letter and needs no answer. A failing hook on either is one warning line and compaction goes on. compact.json records `by` (brain, or the hook that gave the summary) and, after a block, `phase: blocked` with the hook's name. To hook one: self_hook add with event before_compact or after_compact (aos/me.json#/self_hook).
- An empty summary or one with tool calls is unusable. The body removes the request, drops the /compact letters as failed, and keeps the prior conversation. Brain failures follow the ordinary cooldown/stop rules. Do not claim compaction succeeded without the summary and compact done rows.
- Open do_task start marks may be folded away. A later do_task end then closes the task with MarkerMissing and folds nothing; this is expected, not a reason to retry end. The body does not edit tasks.json.
- With --history task, the summary request still gets the full history. After folding, an applicable summary is included when intervening assistant rows are only compact done rows (aos.compact is true). A mid-turn continuation resumes directly without an idle goal reminder. Idle compaction leaves normal goal reminders enabled.
- New agent-fsm definitions enable context_wrap on_clock every 5000 ms with config {"percent":35,"wrap":false}. At the limit it sends /compact directly: the summary is the handoff, with no separate wrap-up answer.
- The fsm reading is the last valid think usage.prompt_tokens divided by the endpoint pack context published by the kernel. If prompt_tokens is absent, input_tokens plus cache_read_input_tokens plus cache_creation_input_tokens is used. Completion tokens are not counted. A compact observation is not a think reading. config.window overrides the pack context; without either window or valid usage, the hook does nothing.
- To change the threshold, edit config.percent (1 to 100) in the context_wrap hook entry, or add it again with self_hook add, replace true and the whole config, keeping wrap false: {"op":"add","event":"on_clock","every_ms":5000,"name":"context_wrap","path_json":{"$env":"AOS_HOME","$path":"/lib/tools/agent/context_wrap"},"config":{"percent":50,"wrap":false},"timeout_ms":20000,"replace":true} (aos/me/self_hook.json#/answer). An authorized manager can write the hook entry with JSON tools. To turn off the automatic hook, use self_hook {"op":"rm","name":"context_wrap"} if available, or have the manager set your stack's hookeds.json#/context_wrap to null. This does not disable manual /compact.
- context_wrap --reading <stack> prints the reading or why none is available. Compaction does not repeat while the hook stays compacted; a later ordinary think reading must be below the threshold to rearm it. Long-running tools are checked only after the step ends; a single oversized tool result cannot be rescued by this hook. Summary quality depends on the model: consult the retained original letters, history_removed.jsonl, or handoff.md when needed.
